needsHuman.title: Kids always have control
needsHuman.reason: No pause button, mute button, or quit/home control is visible on any screen (menu, playing, failing, or winning) — only debug FPS/position text, control instructions, and (on the win screen) a "Play again" button are shown; failing itself only costs a little progress (back to the maze start), which is fine, but the missing pause/mute/quit controls fail the rule.

findings.summary: Claude fail: No pause button, mute button, or quit/home control is visible on any screen (menu, playing, failing, or winning) — only debug FPS/position text, control instructions, and (on the win screen) a "Play again" button are shown; failing itself only costs a little progress (back to the maze start), which is fine, but the missing pause/mute/quit controls fail the rule.

Claude warn: The controls panel is one instruction a child must parse, but it's ~25 words with key names, arrow symbols, and abbreviations ("W/↑ Forward | S/↓ Back A/← Strafe Left | D/→ Strafe Right Mouse to Look Around Touch: drag left side to move, right side to look") — far over 5 words. The spike message "Ouch! A spike sent you back to the start." is 8 words. Only "You found the way out!" (5 words) and "Level 1" (2 words) fit the threshold.

Claude fail: Source shows 0 audio files, no speechSynthesis, no WebAudio, and no <audio> elements — none of the on-screen text (controls, spike message, win message) is spoken or replayable, which this bracket requires for early/non-readers.

rules.title: No blood
rules.reason: No blood, splatter or bleed wording anywhere; the only red is the fail-message UI box, which is explicitly OK as UI colour.

rules.title: No weapons or guns
rules.reason: The only hazard is the static floor spike cluster, an approved environmental hazard, not a weapon; no gun, sword or other weapon appears in any screenshot or text.

rules.title: No bashing or breaking of living things
rules.reason: Nothing animate is bashed or broken; the player just bumps a faceless spike hazard and resets to the start.

rules.title: No injury or death shown
rules.reason: On hitting the spike the game only shows the kind message "Ouch! A spike sent you back to the start." and resets position, with no wound, body, or death wording shown.

rules.title: No harm to animals or creatures
rules.reason: No animals or creatures appear in any screenshot or text.

rules.title: No scary content
rules.reason: The maze is brightly and evenly lit (sky-blue walls, green floor) in every playing shot, and even the dim door-interior winning screen is soft brown, not dark or menacing; no monsters or chases appear.

rules.title: No meanness
rules.reason: The only failure text, "Ouch! A spike sent you back to the start.", is a kind exclamation with no insult or mockery.

rules.title: No stereotypes
rules.reason: No characters, costumes, accents, or group-based jokes appear anywhere; the game has no human or cultural depictions at all.

rules.title: No romance, sexual content, drugs, alcohol, tobacco or vaping
rules.reason: No romance, sexual content, or drug/alcohol/tobacco/vape imagery appears in any screenshot or text.

rules.title: No bad language
rules.reason: All visible text ("Ouch! A spike sent you back to the start.", "You found the way out!", "Play again", control instructions) is clean, with no swearing or crude insults.

rules.title: No dangerous stunts a kid could copy
rules.reason: No real-life-copyable dangerous stunts (fire, outlets, medicine, unsafe climbing) are shown or rewarded; the maze and spike hazard are clearly fantastical game elements.

rules.title: No gambling or casino-style mechanics
rules.reason: No spin-the-wheel, loot box, or chance-based reward mechanic appears; the only outcome shown is a fixed "You found the way out!" win state with a "Play again" choice.

rules.title: No money, ads or data
rules.reason: No prices, store, ads, sign-in/account screen, personal-data prompt, chat, or outbound links appear anywhere; only a local FPS/position debug overlay and game UI are shown.

rules.title: No manipulative design
rules.reason: There is no countdown, streak, energy timer, or guilt-trip button; on winning, the child gets a plain optional "Play again" button with no forced autoplay into a next level.

rules.title: Safe for the senses
rules.reason: Screenshots show flat, evenly lit scenes with no strobing or rapid colour changes, and the source has zero audio files, so no sudden loud sound is possible.

checks.title: Time pressure
checks.reason: No visible timer, countdown, or racing opponent in any screenshot; the FPS counter is a dev stat, not player-facing pressure. Play is self-paced.

checks.title: Failing
checks.reason: On touching the spike the player is already back at the start position (2.5, 0.0, 2.5, matching menu-start.png) by the first failing screenshot, so retry is instant, not a multi-second delay. Wording is soft ("sent you back to the start", no death/lose language). Minor note: the bold red banner and "Ouch!" reads a bit alarming for the youngest kids even though the mechanic itself is gentle — consider a softer color/word (e.g. a yellow "Oops! Back to the start").

checks.title: Things on screen at once
checks.reason: At most ~4-5 competing elements at once (FPS/Position box, Controls box, Level badge, plus the spike hazard or a message banner) — within the 5-6 target. Worth flagging: the FPS/Position debug overlay (e.g. "Position: 7.5, 0.0, 2.5") looks like leftover dev-tooling rather than something meant for a young child and adds visual noise; recommend hiding it in the kid-facing build.

checks.title: Scariness
checks.reason: Low-poly, brightly colored environment (sky blue, green grass) with a geometric grey spike trap rather than a menacing creature; the win screen's dim brown vignette around the door is moody but not threatening. Overall reads as mild, cartoon-level peril appropriate for 5-7.

checks.title: Contrast
checks.reason: Text panels use white/light-grey text on solid dark backgrounds (Controls box, FPS/Position box, Level badge, red Ouch! banner, win message) — all comfortably above 4.5:1. The spike hazard is distinguished by its shape/silhouette, not color alone, so no information relies on color perception.
